observed: Three steps completed normally, with 33 prefix records reported matching the saved v5 trajectory.
All three liquid peaks lie in the same interface-height layer, at alphaLiquid approximately 0.49485, with downward liquid and upward gas velocity.
The last two global liquid peaks are not direct boundary-face owners; nearly equal wall-adjacent peaks remain in the same interface-height layer.
Liquid bulk peak is approximately 0.07084 mm/s at 0.15 ms, versus 0.80010 mm/s for present-liquid peak.
Whole-domain volume-mixture RMS reaches approximately 1.48264 mm/s, so the quieter bulk liquid alone does not establish quiescence.
The gas peak is predominantly horizontal: 40.0167 mm/s in the interface and 34.8828 mm/s in the bulk-gas layer above it at 0.15 ms. Neither peak owns a boundary face.
Gas motion away from the liquid-maximum location invalidates a vertical-counterflow-only account of the remaining disturbance.
interpretation.inference: The liquid peaks show normal counterflow on a plausible density-contrast force scale, while the larger gas peaks are predominantly horizontal. Neither observation closes the discrete force budget. A separate single-velocity resolved-interface reference will test the shared mesh/initialization/pressure balance without independent phase slip.
missing: A closed spatial/discrete force budget distinguishing hydrostatic interpolation, interface forces and phase slip.

decision: Build a private observation-only Foundation OF9 interFoam reference, with a single velocity, the unchanged native mesh/1000-L initial fill/p_rgh/gravity and fluid properties. Run at most 10 ms with separate phase-volume budgets and the existing pressure, liquid-speed, fraction, Courant and redistribution limits. This is a resolved-interface hydrodynamic reference, not an accepted dispersed-bubble/PBM/oxygen/biology replacement. Preserve all BiRD controls; change no force coefficient or acceptance threshold.
